charts_title: One Look Tells You *What the Market Is Doing*
charts_sub: Real charts with NiftyMeter added. Watch the coloured band strip at the bottom: **light** colours mean the market is tradeable, **dark** colours and **white** mean wait. Tap each tab to see the three market moods: bullish, bearish and neutral.

charts.name: BULLISH — Green bands
charts.sub: Price is climbing and the bands turn green. Light green is a tradeable zone — look for a buy entry above the previous candle's high, with a stop loss below the recent low.

charts.name: BEARISH — Red bands
charts.sub: Price is falling and the bands turn red. Light red is a tradeable zone on the sell side — avoid fresh buying and exit long trades below the previous candle's low.

charts.name: NEUTRAL — White bands
charts.sub: No clear direction — price moves sideways and the bands stay white. This is a no-trade zone: stay out and wait for light green or light red to return.

signal_cards.title: Green — Bullish · Tradeable
signal_cards.text: Buyers are in control. Look for a buy entry when a candle closes above the previous high, with a stop loss below the recent low.

signal_cards.title: Red — Bearish · Tradeable
signal_cards.text: Sellers are in control. Avoid fresh buying and exit long trades when a candle closes below the previous low.

signal_cards.title: White — Neutral · No trade
signal_cards.text: No clear direction. Do nothing and wait for green or red to return — waiting is also a trade.

faqs.q: I have never traded before. Can I still use NiftyMeter?
faqs.a: Yes — it is built for complete beginners. The learning videos start from zero: what a chart is, what a candle means, and how to read the 5 band colours. You can learn and practise by just watching charts before you put in any money.

faqs.q: What do the band colours mean?
faqs.a:
**Light green** — bullish and tradeable: look for buy entries.
**Dark green** — bullish but not tradeable: hold, don't start new trades.
**Light red** — bearish and tradeable: avoid buying, exit longs.
**Dark red** — bearish but not tradeable: stay out.
**White** — no trade zone: the market is undecided, so wait.

faqs.q: Which timeframes does NiftyMeter work on?
faqs.a: All of them — intraday (1, 3, 5, 15 and 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours) as well as daily, weekly and monthly charts. Beginners should start with daily or weekly charts: signals are slower and calmer, which makes learning easier.

faqs.q: What is TradingView? Do I have to pay for it?
faqs.a: TradingView is a popular charting website and app. A **free** TradingView account is enough to use NiftyMeter — you only need to share the email you sign up with, so we can give you access.

faqs.q: Do I need a demat account to start?
faqs.a: Not for learning. You can watch the videos and practise reading charts without one. When you are ready to place real trades, you will need a demat and trading account with any SEBI-registered broker.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to start?
faqs.a: There is no minimum to learn. When you start trading, begin with a small amount you can afford to lose, and always use a stop loss. Increase your size only after you are consistent.

No tool can guarantee profits — anyone who promises that is not being honest. NiftyMeter helps you see the trend clearly and follow simple rules, including where to cut a loss. Results depend on your discipline and risk management.

faqs.q: What are the 5 strategies? Are they easy to follow?
faqs.a: Yes. They are: (1) Trend Confirmation Entry, (2) Breakout Play, (3) Breakdown Play, (4) Opening Range / Morning Gap, and (5) Pullback Entry. Each one explains the entry, the stop loss and the target in plain language, with chart examples.

faqs.q: What happens after the 7-day free trial?
faqs.a: If you find it useful, you can continue with NiftyMeter (see the Pricing section for the current offer). If not, your access simply stops — no charges, no hassle. We will remind you before the trial ends.
